title: Championship's first six-team play-off race takes shape
excerpt: For the first time, eight Championship clubs can reach the Premier League. Here's how the new play-off format works and who's in the frame.
content_html:
England's Championship has added two extra play-off places this season, giving eight of its 24 clubs a route to the Premier League for the first time.

EFL clubs voted in March to expand the second-tier play-offs from four teams to six from the 2026-27 season. The top two still win automatic promotion, and the next six now fight for the third promotion place.

How the new format works

  • Third and fourth go straight into the semi-finals.
  • Fifth to eighth meet in quarter-finals for the two remaining semi-final spots.
  • The semi-final winners play off in the final at Wembley.

Supporters of the change say it keeps more clubs and fans involved deep into the season. Critics argue it reduces the reward for finishing in the top four.

Where the race stands

After matches played on 25 November, the top of the table is tightly bunched:

  • Middlesbrough: 35 points from 17 games
  • Stoke City: 35 points
  • Wolverhampton Wanderers: 34 points
  • Birmingham City: 32 points
  • West Bromwich Albion: 32 points
  • Southampton: 28 points

Southampton would be higher. The club was docked four points for breaches linked to unauthorised filming of other clubs' training sessions.

Who would have benefited last season

Wrexham are the obvious example. The Welsh club, owned by Hollywood actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, finished seventh in 2025-26 on 71 points, one place outside the old play-off zone. Under this season's rules, seventh is a play-off spot.

Coventry City won the title last season with 95 points.

Pressure at the bottom

The bigger play-off zone has not eased the pressure on struggling clubs. Preston North End sacked Paul Heckingbottom on 13 September with the club 23rd and appointed Graham Alexander two weeks later. Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, dismissed Nicky Hayen on 24 October with the club 22nd and named Fabio Celestini as his replacement four days later.

Why it matters

Promotion to the Premier League is widely estimated to be worth more than £100 million to a club once broadcast income and later parachute payments are counted. Spreading the chance across more teams is likely to raise the stakes in the second half of the season.

With 29 rounds left, the six-team play-off picture is far from settled.
